cards.explanation: The answer is the Wilderness of Sinai, friends! Verse 1 says the LORD spoke to Moses in the Tent of Meeting in the Wilderness of Sinai. Moses is Israel's leader, and he's about to get a very big counting job. Picture it: the whole camp is out in the desert, and the LORD says, 'Take a census.' I'd be nervous, friends. I can't even count the crumbs on my counter without losing my place.
The answer is name. God says to list "…every man by name, one by one." (Numbers 1:2) Not a tally mark, not a guess. A name. I think that's a pretty good sign every man in that crowd counted.

God wants men twenty or older who can serve in the army counted. Verse 3 says to number those twenty years of age or older, everyone who can serve in Israel's army. Both parts matter, friends: the age and the army. Plenty of people in Israel aren't on this list.

The answer is False. God tells Moses, "You and Aaron are to number those…" (Numbers 1:3). Aaron is Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14). And God adds that one man from each tribe, the head of each family, must be there with them (Numbers 1:4). It's a team job, and Moses gets a whole crew.

The answer is True. The LORD gives the order on the first day of the second month (Numbers 1:1). Then Moses and Aaron assemble the whole congregation on the first day of the second month (Numbers 1:18). Same date, friends. They didn't sit on this one, and they didn't hit snooze either.

The answer is tabernacle. God says the Levites are to be appointed over the tabernacle of the Testimony, all its furnishings, and everything in it (Numbers 1:50). So the Levites get a different kind of job than the army. They carry it, care for it, and camp around it.

The answer is True. Verse 51 says whenever the tabernacle is to move, the Levites take it down, and whenever it is to be pitched, the Levites set it up. So taking it down and putting it up are both Levite jobs. I think that's a lot of packing for one tribe.

The answer is that he must be put to death, and it's a heavy one. God says, "Any outsider who goes near it must be put to death." (Numbers 1:51) That's the serious rule He gives for the tabernacle. The text says it plainly, so we do too.

The answer is by divisions under their own standards. God says the Israelites are to camp by their divisions, each man in his own camp and under his own standard (Numbers 1:52). So each group has its own spot and its own flag. No wandering around looking for your tent.

The answer is so no wrath falls on Israel. The Levites camp around the tabernacle of the Testimony and watch over it "…so that no wrath will fall on the congregation of Israel." (Numbers 1:53) So the Levites' watch is for the whole congregation, friends. The reason comes straight from God's own words.

The answer is True, and that's how the chapter ends. Verse 54 says, "Thus the Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses." That's a whole census, a camp plan and a job for the Levites, all carried out as commanded. Not bad for a crowd of over six hundred thousand men.
